description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects: The Project is expected to contribute to increased access to finance for women-owned SMEs and climate finance for SMEs in South Africa. Despite having a developed financial sector, SMEs in South Africa still experience challenges in accessing credit, mainly from insufficient collateral or guarantees required by the banks. By providing FRB with a long-term de-risking instrument, the Project is expected to contribute to bridging this gap and increase access to finance for SMEs, especially in these two underserved segments.
Contribution to market creation: This Project is part of a program of interventions that IFC is pursuing with several financial institutions to expand their climate finance lending capacity in South Africa. Within this broader programmatic approach, this project particularly targets SMEs, which are looking for financing to mitigate climate risks and increase resilience of their business. This would include SMEs with climate-smart agriculture projects. Within climate finance, supporting climate smart agricultural practices is an important step towards driving transformation in South Africa's agriculture sector, which is particularly at risk of climate change (due to increased events of floods and droughts in recent years). Beyond climate finance, the Project also targets WSMEs which remains an underserved segment. This Project will further promote market replication, especially on adaptation and resilience finance for SMEs.

The proposed project consists of an unfunded Risk Sharing Facility (RSF) to FirstRand Bank Limited (FRB or the Bank) where IFC will cover 50% of the credit risk of an up to US$100 million equivalent in South African Rand (ZAR) portfolio of eligible loans to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in South Africa (the Project). The RSF will specifically support the Bank to finance woman-owned SMEs and SMEs involved with climate solutions, including climate smart agriculture; or healthcare activities. The Project will be processed under the Small Loan Guarantee Program European Commission/Private Sector Window (SLGP EC/PSW or the Program), a programmatic approach to risk sharing which aims to enhance and strengthen the capacity of financial institutions for risk taking and financing of SMEs in eligible countries. The Project is also expected to be supported by the IFC-BMWK (Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Klimaschutz) Scale Up Climate Finance through Greening the Financial Sector (BMWK) Program as described in the Blended Finance section.
